findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders of every method
findings.body: The new deleteMany ORs the old past-due SMS cleanup with retryCount > 1, and that second predicate has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP. On the next run of this SMS cron, any row with retryCount greater than 1 is deleted, including email and WhatsApp reminders and SMS rows already marked scheduled with a Twilio referenceId. Deleting a scheduled row drops the referenceId used to cancel the queued text, so a later booking cancellation cannot stop the message. The comment above the query still says it only removes past SMS reminders, which is no longer true. Scope the retry branch to unscheduled SMS (method SMS and scheduled false).

findings.title: Two failures of any kind permanently drop the SMS
findings.body: retryCount is incremented both when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value and for every exception in the surrounding try, including template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, and database lookups, not only Twilio rejections. The next cron then deletes the row once retryCount > 1. Permanent failures (invalid number) and transient ones (Twilio 5xx, rate limit, network, brief DB error) share that budget, with no backoff beyond the cron interval. Two failures close together therefore remove the reminder even if the event is still days away, so a short provider outage can silently drop every SMS reminder in the 7-day window. Only non-retryable errors should exhaust the counter; transient errors need more attempts or a delay before deletion.

findings.title: Missing number or empty body never consumes retries
findings.body: retryCount is only updated when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the message body is empty, the code skips the send and does not increment retryCount or delete the row. Those reminders stay scheduled=false and are loaded, and their templates rebuilt, on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded retry this PR is meant to stop, for a permanent failure that will never succeed. Treat that skip as a failed attempt or delete the row.

findings.title: Retry-count update in catch aborts the rest of the batch
findings.body: The new workflowReminder.update inside the per-reminder catch is not guarded. If it throws — the row was already deleted because the booking was cancelled, or the database errors — the exception escapes the catch, the original scheduling error is never logged, and the for-loop stops. Every later reminder in this invocation is skipped. Previously a single reminder failure was logged and the handler continued. If scheduleSMS had already accepted the message and the follow-up update failed, this path also counts that as a retry failure without saving referenceId, so the queued text can no longer be cancelled. The retry update needs its own try/catch so one row cannot fail the batch.

findings.title: Overlapping crons can delete a reminder Twilio already accepted
findings.body: Failures write retryCount to the in-memory value plus one instead of an atomic increment, and the cleanup delete removes any row with retryCount > 1 even when scheduled is already true. The handler never claims the row before calling Twilio, so overlapping cron runs can interleave: one run fails and stores retryCount 2, while the other run's scheduleSMS succeeds and sets scheduled and referenceId without clearing retryCount. Partial updates do not reset the other field, so the next run deletes that row. The Twilio message stays queued, but the referenceId required to cancel it is gone. Use an atomic increment and only delete unscheduled SMS rows.

findings.title: retryCount cleanup sequentially scans WorkflowReminder
findings.body: Every cron invocation deletes rows with retryCount > 1, but the new predicate is not covered by the existing indexes on (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, or (cancelled, scheduledDate). Postgres must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder on each run, even when almost no rows match. On a bookings-scale table that scan is repeated for the life of the cron. Add an index that matches the cleanup filter (for example method plus retryCount) if this delete stays.

findings.title: No test locks the retry delete scope or threshold
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive delete and a failure counter with no tests. Nothing asserts that an email or WhatsApp reminder with retryCount > 1 is kept, that an already scheduled SMS row is kept, that a missing phone number does not spin until the event date, or that an SMS reminder is removed only after two failures and not on the first. Those are the branches this change gets wrong, and a fixture test of the delete filter and the increment paths would have caught them.
